title: 知识为何留得住：主动回忆与间隔重复
topic: How learning sticks: active recall and spaced repetition

sentences.en: Today I want to raise a question every teacher on this faculty keeps asking: why do students forget so much of what we teach?
sentences.zh: 今天我想提一个我们这个教师群体里每位老师都反复追问的问题：为什么学生会忘掉我们教的那么多东西？

sentences.en: For a long time, our pedagogy assumed that if a professor gives a clear lecture and students stay attentive, the knowledge will simply stick.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，我们的教学法都假定：只要教授把课讲清楚、学生又听得专注，知识自然就会记住。

sentences.en: But cognitive psychology tells a different story: human cognition treats memory not as a recording, but as something you rebuild.
sentences.zh: 但认知心理学讲的是另一回事：人的认知并不把记忆当成录像，而是当成你要重新建构的东西。

sentences.en: So passively listening, or rereading the syllabus, feels productive but does little for long-term retention.
sentences.zh: 所以被动听讲，或把大纲反复读一遍，感觉很有成效，却对长期的记忆保持没什么用。

sentences.en: The most powerful move is not to memorize passively, but to practice active recall: close the book and force yourself to retrieve the answer.
sentences.zh: 最有力的做法不是被动死记，而是练习主动回忆：合上书，逼自己把答案取出来。

sentences.en: Every time you struggle to retain a fact and pull it back, that retrieval reinforces the memory—which is why a quiz is not just an assessment: being tested is itself learning.
sentences.zh: 每次你费力地想记住一个知识点又把它拉回来，这种提取都会强化记忆——这正是为什么测验不只是评估：被测试本身就是一种学习。

sentences.en: The second principle is spaced repetition: review after a day, a week, then a month, so each review lands as you begin to forget.
sentences.zh: 第二条原理是间隔重复：隔一天、隔一周、再隔一个月复习，让每次复习都恰好落在你快要遗忘的时候。

sentences.en: Cramming the night before an exam raises a score once, but spaced practice builds understanding that lasts for years.
sentences.zh: 考前一晚临时抱佛脚只能让分数一时上去，但间隔练习建立的理解能持续好几年。

sentences.en: None of this works without timely feedback: when a learner quickly hears whether an answer was right and why, they comprehend the rule behind it.
sentences.zh: 这一切也离不开及时反馈：学习者很快得知答案对不对、为什么，就能领会背后的规则。

sentences.en: This is where a small seminar or a session with a tutor beats a big lecture hall: you perceive your mistakes at once.
sentences.zh: 这时，小型研讨课或跟导师的一对一辅导就胜过大讲堂：你能立刻察觉自己的错误。

sentences.en: Underneath it all sits motivation: a scholarship or a grade can motivate a student briefly, but intrinsic motivation—genuine curiosity—predicts more durable learning.
sentences.zh: 而这一切的底层是动机：奖学金或分数能短暂地激励学生，但内在动机——真正的好奇心——才更能预示更持久的学习。

sentences.en: Aptitude still matters—some learners pick up a new discipline faster—but good strategy narrows the gap, and skills like literacy grow mainly through practice.
sentences.zh: 天资仍然重要——有些学习者上手一门新学科更快——但好的策略能缩小差距，而读写能力这类技能主要靠练习长出来。

sentences.en: So don't just list topics on a curriculum and hope for the best; that kind of instruction leaves too much to chance.
sentences.zh: 所以别只把主题列在课程大纲上就指望学好——那样的教学把太多东西交给了运气。

sentences.en: Build in retrieval, space it out, give fast feedback, and protect motivation—then enrollment turns into real, lasting understanding.
sentences.zh: 把提取练习嵌进去、拉开间隔、给出快速反馈、并保护好动机——注册入学就会变成真实而持久的理解。
